documents.title: Department of Computer Science Policies for Using Generative AI (GAI) and Large Language Models (LLMs)
documents.stance_why: The default policy says AI "may not be used as a wholesale substitute", allows narrow uses (brainstorming, exam preparation, polishing text), and says AI "may be used in undergraduate classes if and only if the instructor permits it in writing". AI is therefore banned unless permitted, with a short list of acceptable uses, which is restrict.
documents.summary: The CS department sets a default AI policy for all its courses and academic work: attribute AI use, never use it as a wholesale substitute for solutions, code or writing, and use it only for limited things like brainstorming or polishing text. Instructors may set their own policy, but in undergraduate courses AI is allowed only with written instructor permission and Undergraduate Program Director approval. Students must be able to explain their work unaided.

documents.title: Technology, AI and Society's Policy for Using Generative AI (GAI) & Large Language Models (LLMs)
documents.stance_why: The seven general rules say AI "may be used for brainstorming ideas, for exam preparation" and "to polish text", require attribution, and ban only a "wholesale substitute" for student work. AI is allowed with conditions, which is permit.
documents.summary: The department adopts seven default rules for courses and research: attribute AI use with software, version and prompts, no wholesale substitution of student work, very limited use in theses, and allowed uses such as brainstorming, exam preparation and polishing text. Students must be able to explain their work in their own words. Custom instructor policies must be published and approved by the program director in undergraduate courses.

units.why: The department "has adopted a policy on the use of Generative AI and Large Language Models" in courses, research and academic activities and says it applies to "all DTAS academic contexts", so a scope statement (P56).
units.anchor: adopted a policy on the use of Generative AI and Large Language Models

units.why: "Aligned with university-wide guidelines" says the policy is consistent with the university guidance; no type covers alignment with a higher-level policy.
units.anchor: Aligned with university-wide guidelines
units.uncovered_note: The department policy states it is aligned with the university-wide guidelines.

units.why: The policy "provides clear guidance to promote responsible use, uphold academic integrity, and prevent ethical issues", a stated purpose grounded in integrity, so P95 with a fit note.
units.anchor: provides clear guidance to promote responsible use, uphold academic integrity, and prevent ethical issues
units.fit_note: Purpose also includes responsible use and ethics, not only integrity.

units.why: "will be updated regularly to reflect technological developments" commits to revising the policy, so P54.
units.anchor: will be updated regularly to reflect technological developments

units.why: "AI tools are intended to support—not replace—students’ independent reasoning and understanding" says students must remain the primary thinker, so P32.
units.anchor: AI tools are intended to support—not replace—students’ independent reasoning and understanding

units.why: "The seven general rules are the default DTAS AI policy for courses and other department work" states what applies by default when an instructor sets none, so P06.

units.fit_note: A default for all courses, with instructors allowed to publish custom policies, rather than a rule for silent syllabi specifically.

units.why: "All instructors who wish to define their own custom AI policy must publish it on their class website, in syllabi" requires written communication of custom policies, so P09.
